Hi Helen / procurement team —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Per our conversation, I’m attaching a set of simulations that map expected token throughput to plan tiers (compact, core, dedicated-burst) plus two downgrade/credit scenarios. High level: we see three practical paths that match the traffic profiles you described.

Attachments: clearline-tier-simulations.xlsx (tabbed: baseline, growth-3yr, downgrade-paths)

Key asks before we lock a recommendation:
- Confirm expected Q4 peak concurrency (tokens/sec or requests/min) — you mentioned a 2.5x seasonal uplift.
- Which features must remain enabled (structured output, tool-calling, KV-cache persists) if you downgrade?
- Procurement question: would Clearline accept prorated credits for unused reserved capacity during a 90-day downgrade window, or do you need seat carryforward?

Suggested next step: 60-minute workshop with Redwoods’ Finance + Sales Ops + your procurement + product manager to walk the scenarios and agree on a guardrail (prorate vs credit vs fee). I can run two short demos in the session showing latency/cost tradeoffs for compact vs core with quantization.

- Wed 9/23 14:00–15:00
- Thu 9/24 09:00–10:00

If none of those work, propose alternatives and I’ll adjust. I’ve looped in Aditya (pricing) and Jonas (sales ops) here; they’ll bring the scenario-level numbers and sample amendment language.

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the simulations — looks helpful. A couple quick clarifying questions before we pull in procurement ops: 

1) On downgrade credits: does Redwood offer a prorated refund for reserved capacity if we move down within the first 6 months, or is the standard approach an account credit we can apply to other Redwood consumption?
2) Seat carryforward: our CFO prefers credits over straight refunds; can credits be used against hosted API usage (not just future reserved capacity)?
3) If we pick a compact-tier for cost reasons and later experience latency regressions for certain inference-heavy routes, is there a documented step to temporarily burst to core/dedicated without re-signing? What are the SLA implications?

I’ll loop in our Head of Procurement for the workshop. For timing, Wed 9/23 14:00–15:00 looks promising. Can you include a short one-pager with amendment language that outlines the downgrade window and credit math?

Marissa / Aditya —

Quick takeaways to prepare for Helen’s procurement team. I ran three compact scenarios against Clearline’s baseline traffic (per the spreadsheet) and sketched the amendment language. Sending the raw numbers here so we can finalize the one-pager: 

Scenario A — Conservative (start compact):
- Start: Compact tier (meters + KV-cache)
- Expected monthly tokens: 1.2B
- Latency p95: 180–220ms (compact quantized path)
- Downgrade window: 90 days post-commit; unused reserved capacity credited as account credit (usable against hosted API or future reserved purchases)
- Financial impact: 18% lower monthly invoice vs core; estimated savings $26k/mo first year

Scenario B — Balanced (core with burst):
- Start: Core tier, enable scheduled burst to dedicated for heavy inference routes
- Expected monthly tokens: 2.3B
- Latency p95: 90–130ms (core + burst)
- Downgrade window: 180 days; prorated credits for unused months (applied as account credit)
- Financial impact: baseline pricing; better SLA during peak

Scenario C — Throughput-first (dedicated-reserve):
- Start: Dedicated-reserved pool with autoscale; includes faster KV persistence
- Expected monthly tokens: 4.8B
- Latency p95: <75ms for pinned routes
- Downgrade path: requires 30-day notice and an amendment (fee applies for early termination)
- Financial impact: higher fixed cost but predictable unit price for high throughput

Notes for the workshop one-pager:
- We should offer credits that are usable across product surfaces (hosted API or future reserved capacity) — aligns with Helen’s CFO preference.
- Include an explicit temporary burst option (automated routing to core or dedicated for flagged endpoints) as a documented fallback; no re-sign required for short bursts, but SLA tiers differ.
- Draft a short amendment template (DocuSign-ready) that contains: downgrade window, credit math, burst policy, and termination fees for dedicated-reserved.

I’ll draft the one-pager and amendment template. Marissa — do you want me to include the exact credit formula (pro rata by remaining full-months * committed $) or keep it simple for procurement?

—Jonas

Hi Helen —

Thanks — quick update and attachments as requested. I’ve attached the one-pager and the draft amendment (DocuSign-ready). Answers inline to your earlier questions: 

1) Refunds vs credits: Redwood’s standard for reserved-capacity downgrades is to issue account credits for unused committed dollars (credit applies to hosted API or future reserved purchases). We can offer a prorated refund for deals over $250k ARR on a case-by-case basis — I’ve flagged that as an option in the amendment.

2) Seat carryforward: credits are the default. We can include a clause to allow seat carryforward for the first renewal only if procurement requires it; this is a limited exception.

3) Temporary burst without re-signing: supported. We include an automated routing policy to burst selected routes to core/dedicated for up to 14 days with immediate billing at burst rates; no new signature needed for bursts under the agreed threshold. SLA implications will be spelled out in section 2 of the amendment (short bursts receive best-effort latency SLO; sustained bursts > 30 days escalate to dedicated-reserve negotiation).

Next steps:
- Confirm workshop slot: Wed 9/23 14:00–15:00 PDT — I’ll send a calendar invite when you confirm.
- Review attached proposal and amendment draft and call out any redlines before the workshop.
- If procurement wants, we can pre-populate the DocuSign with the provisional credit math (I’ve included a sample formula in the PDF).

Links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/CL-2026-0917 | DocuSign draft: https://docusign.com/CL-2026-0917

Attachments: proposal-CL-2026-0917.pdf, clearline-tier-simulations.xlsx, docusign-term-amendment-CL-2026-0917.pdf

Best,
